summary.text: 下 is an indicative character: an early short mark below a longer line shows the position “below.” Later forms add a descending stroke, but accounts disagree about when it appeared and whether the upper line represents a general reference or the horizon.

formation.text: Indicative (指事). Early forms place a short stroke below a longer reference line to mark “below.” One account identifies the longer line as the horizon; another treats it more generally as a reference line. This is a whole-graph analysis, not a compound of separate sound and meaning components.

history.text: The curated seal-style image is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact. It shows a short lower stroke and a descending vertical stroke; the sources explain the addition as distinguishing 下 from 上 and 二. They disagree on whether the vertical was established in late Spring and Autumn forms or in small seal script, and the supplied evidence does not settle the date.

The received 說文解字 entry describes 丅 as an indicative graph meaning “bottom” and calls 下 its seal-script form. This is a transmitted dictionary analysis, not direct evidence for the shape or date of the Shang graph.

uncertainties.text: The graphic accounts differ both on what the long upper line represents and when the lower mark became a descending vertical stroke. No dated specimen in this dossier resolves either point.

The dossier reports competing proposals for the spoken word’s deeper etymology, but they were not independently verified here. They concern the spoken word and do not determine how the graph was formed.

senses.text: The graph is interpreted as indicating a lower position. Cited oracle-bone uses refer to lower deities and ancestral spirits; the evidence attests these uses but does not establish that either was the character’s original meaning.
A cited bronze inscription uses 下 in reference to the human world below.

senses.period: Later transmitted texts; precise date unresolved
senses.text: Later cited texts use 下 as a verb meaning “descend.” The evidence does not date this use within a complete sequence of meaning changes.

senses.text: The dossier cites a later use expressing humility toward a superior, but does not establish when or through what steps it developed from the lower-position sense.

senses.period: Warring States text; precise date unresolved
senses.text: A cited military passage uses 下 for a city that does not surrender or fall. The supplied account does not establish a semantic path from “below” to this use.

developments.text: The bronze use for the human world below is consistent with applying the lower-position sense to a domain beneath an upper one.
The verb “descend” is compatible with movement toward a lower position, but the dossier does not document the transition’s chronology.

limitations.text: The cited examples attest several uses but do not provide a complete dated sequence connecting “below,” “descend,” humility, and “capture.” These uses should not be treated as a proven chain of meaning change.
The dossier lists historical readings and competing spoken-word etymology proposals, but does not establish a connection between them and the character’s graphic formation.

overview.text: A short mark below a longer line indicates “below.” Later forms add a downward stroke, though its date is disputed. The evidence also records uses for lower deities and the world below.
